question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

When someone waves a white flag, it signifies that they **__want to tolerate__** to the other party.
solution:
The correct answer is **"want to surrender."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"wave a white flag"** is a common idiom that means to surrender or give up. (समर्पण करना या छोड़ देना)

 
 
• **Example**: *The worker finally **waves the white flag**__ in defeat.*
 
 
 
• **"Want to tolerate"** does not make sense in this context as the person waving the white flag is not trying to tolerate anything.
 
• **"Want to interrupt"** and **"wanted to interrogate" **are both incorrect as they do not relate to the act of waving a white flag.
 
• **"Surrender"** means to stop fighting and admit that you have lost. (लड़ना बंद कर अपनी हार मान लेना, आत्‍मसमर्पण कर देना)
 __
 
• **Example**: *The hijackers eventually **wanted to surrender**__ themselves to the police.*
 
 
 
• The correct option, **"want to surrender",** accurately reflects the meaning of the idiom.
 
• The correct answer is Option 4.
